title: My city
subtitle: Omar writes about Amman — comparatives and superlatives together
canDo: I can describe my city: its size, weather, places and food.
I can use comparatives and superlatives together in a text.
I can write a short article for a school newsletter.
teacherNotes: Bu ders bir yazma dersi: okuma metnindeki sıra (yer, ünlü olduğu şey, hava, yemek, en sevilen yer) öğrencilerin kendi metninin planı olur.
much + comparative (much bigger) ve one of the + superlative + çoğul isim (one of the oldest cities) en sık yapılan hatalar.
Amman yedi tepe üzerine kurulmuştur; şehir merkezindeki Roma tiyatrosu yaklaşık 1850 yıllık. Arap öğrenciler kendi şehirlerinden benzer bilgiler ekleyebilir.
İzmir ile ilgili bilgiler: Türkiye'nin üçüncü büyük şehri, 3000 yıldan eski; Kordon deniz kenarındaki yürüyüş yolu.

sections.title: Listen and read
sections.heading: Twelve degrees and sunny
sections.scene: Sunday afternoon. Elif and Zeynep are on a video call.

lines.speaker: zeynep
lines.text: Elif! It's nine o'clock at night here. What time is it in Boston?

lines.speaker: elif
lines.text: Two in the afternoon. And it's minus three degrees!

lines.speaker: zeynep
lines.text: Minus three? Here it's twelve degrees and sunny. Winters in Izmir are much milder.

lines.speaker: elif
lines.text: I know. But Boston has snow. It's the most beautiful thing in winter.

lines.speaker: zeynep
lines.text: Is Boston as big as Izmir?

lines.speaker: elif
lines.text: No, it isn't. Izmir is much bigger. About four million people live there, and only 650,000 people live in Boston.

lines.speaker: zeynep
lines.text: Really? I thought Boston was bigger!

lines.speaker: elif
lines.text: It feels big because it's so busy. And Izmir is much older. Boston is only about four hundred years old.

lines.speaker: zeynep
lines.text: So what's the best thing about Boston?

lines.speaker: elif
lines.text: The libraries. And Sam's cookies, of course. What's the best thing about Izmir?

lines.speaker: zeynep
lines.text: The sea, the sunsets … and me!

lines.speaker: elif
lines.text: Ha! You're right. You're the best thing in Izmir.

items.statement: It's warmer in Boston than in Izmir.
For Elif, the libraries are one of the best things about Boston.

sections.title: Read
sections.heading: My city: Amman
sections.intro: A new series in the school newsletter. This week: Omar Haddad.
paragraphs: Amman is the capital of Jordan, and it's my home. About four million people live there, so it's much bigger than Boston. But it isn't as big as Cairo or Istanbul.
Amman is famous for its hills. The old city was built on seven hills, and today there are many more.
Walking in Amman is harder than walking in Boston: you go up and down all day! But from the top of a hill, the views are the best in the world. I'm not joking.
Amman is also one of the oldest cities in the world. In the center, there's an ancient Roman theater. It's almost two thousand years old, much older than any building in Boston.
The weather is drier and sunnier than here. Summers are hot, but the evenings are cooler because the city is high. In winter, it sometimes snows, but not as much as in Boston.
The most famous dish is mansaf: rice and meat with a yogurt sauce. But for me, the best food in Amman is my grandmother's maqluba.
My favorite place is the Citadel at sunset. You can see the whole city from there, and you can hear the call to prayer from hundreds of mosques at the same time.

options: There are a lot of hills.

sections.title: Grammar: comparing places
look: The views are **the best** in the world.
It's **one of the oldest cities** in the world.

head: Structure
Example
rows: It **doesn't snow as much as** in Boston.

rules: Use **much** or **a lot** before a comparative for a big difference: *much bigger*, *a lot cheaper*.
Don't use *very* with a comparative: *much colder* (not *very colder*).
After **one of the** + superlative, the noun is plural: *one of the best **cities***.
examples: Izmir is much warmer than Boston in winter.
It's one of the oldest cities in the world.
My town isn't as busy as the capital.
The best time to visit is in the spring.

support.tr: Bir şehri anlatırken üç yapı birlikte kullanılır: -er / more … than (daha), as … as (kadar), the …-est / the most (en). Farkı büyütmek için much: much bigger = çok daha büyük (very bigger denmez). one of the best cities = en iyi şehirlerden biri: isim çoğul olur.
support.ar: عند وصف مدينة نستخدم: ‎-er‎ / more … than (أكثر من)، as … as (مثل)، the …-est / the most (الأكثر). لتكبير الفرق نستخدم much: much bigger = أكبر بكثير (ولا نقول very bigger). one of the best cities = من أفضل المدن: الاسم بعدها جمع.

tr.note: very + comparative olmaz; one of the'den sonra isim çoğul.
wrong: Amman is very bigger than Boston.
It's one of the best city in the world.
right: Amman is much bigger than Boston.
It's one of the best cities in the world.

ar.note: لا نستخدم very مع المقارنة، والاسم بعد one of the جمع.
wrong: Boston is very colder than Amman.
Petra is one of the most beautiful place in Jordan.
right: Boston is much colder than Amman.
Petra is one of the most beautiful places in Jordan.

sections.title: Practice
sections.instructions: Complete with the correct form of the adjective.
items: Izmir is {warmer} than Boston in winter. (warm)

The traffic is {worse} in the evening than in the morning. (bad)
The Kordon is {the most popular} place for a walk in Izmir. (popular)
Istanbul is much {more crowded} than Izmir. (crowded)

sections.title: Write: My city

model.heading: My city: Izmir — Elif Kaya
text: Izmir is on the west coast of Turkey. About four million people live there, so it's the third biggest city in the country.
It's famous for the sea and the sunsets. The best place for a walk is the Kordon, next to the sea.
Izmir is more than three thousand years old: much older than Boston!
Winters are much milder than here, and summers are very hot.
The best food? A Turkish breakfast with olives, cheese and tea, on a Sunday morning with my family.
My favorite place is my grandmother's balcony. You can see the sea from there.
